parties.petitioner_plaintiff: P.F.Lorence, Commercial Tax Inspector; A.R DAS, Commercial Tax Inspector
parties.respondent_defendant: State Of Kerala, represented by Public Prosecutor

facts_of_case: Petitioners implicated and arraigned as accused in Crime No.335 of 2013. Allegation is that they received cheques or Demand Drafts in violation of Government Order, which were later found to be bounced or forged.

legal_principles.principle: Custodial interrogation is not necessary if the investigating officer has already seized relevant documents.
legal_principles.held: The Investigating Officer has already seized the relevant documents including the questioned cheques and Demand Drafts. Interrogation of the petitioners in custody is not necessary, because even otherwise necessary materials have

legal_principles.principle: A person is not liable under Section 420 IPC if they did not benefit from the alleged crime.
legal_principles.held: The State must fairly concede that these petitioners are not in fact liable under Section 420 IPC. Admittedly, none of the accused was in any manner benefited by the alleged crime.

outcome.final_order: Custodial interrogation not necessary as part of investigation. Petitioners are not liable under Section 420 IPC.

use_for_drafting: seeking pre-arrest bail for commercial tax inspectors
